title: Force as the last resort
hook: peace first; force only when every other means has failed

segments.voice: Yesterday, women in the teaching: why call her bad, from whom kings are born? Your line was equals.

A letter in Persian verse, sent to an emperor. The man who wrote it had lost his father to that empire's executioner, and had lost his sons too. He had every reason to write in pure rage. Instead the letter does something slower. It reminds the emperor of oaths he swore and broke. It talks about God, and about what a ruler owes the people. And in the middle comes one line Sikhs still carry, about when a sword may be lifted at all. The letter is the Zafarnama, from Guru Gobind Singh, and you met it early on this path. Today, that one line, up close.
screen: `A LETTER IN PERSIAN VERSE.` → `TO AN EMPEROR WHO BROKE HIS OATHS.` → `ONE LINE ABOUT THE SWORD.`

segments.voice: First, the line. In paraphrase, the Zafarnama says: when every other means has been tried and has failed, then it is right to take the sword in hand. Notice the order. The sword is not the first word. It's what's left when the other words have run out. Second, what comes before it: talking, bargaining, promises taken in good faith, patience. Tradition says the Guru's side had trusted sworn oaths before they were broken. The letter isn't a war cry; it's a reckoning, and its first weapon is the truth said plainly to power. Third, the person who holds the sword. A salok of Guru Tegh Bahadur, the Guru's father, near the very end of the Granth, says in paraphrase: the one who frightens no one, and is frightened of no one, is the wise one. Not frightened: the courage to stand. Frightening no one: no taste for bullying, no swagger. Initiated Sikhs carry the kirpan, the small sword, as a sign of that pairing, and Sikhs explain it as a duty to protect, not a license to threaten. Fourth, an ordinary Tuesday. Most days nobody reaches for a sword. But the order still applies to a raised voice, a cutting email, a slammed door. Peace first, talk first, truth first, plainly said. The hard part is honesty about the word every. It's easy to say you tried everything after trying one thing twice.
screen: `ZAFARNAMA: ONLY WHEN ALL ELSE FAILS.` · `FIRST: WORDS, PATIENCE, TRUTH.` · `FRIGHTEN NONE, FEAR NONE.` · `THE ORDER ON AN ORDINARY DAY.` · then, large: `PEACE FIRST.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one conflict that's live for you right now, big or small, and notice the part of you that wants to swing first. Then, breath by breath, list the gentler ways still untried: a calmer conversation, a question instead of a charge, a letter rather than a shout, a third person to help. Let one of them settle as the next step.
Force as the last resort. The Zafarnama's teaching that the sword is lifted only when every other means has failed; frighten no one, fear no one. Today's word.
screen: `FORCE AS THE LAST RESORT — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: peace first. Frighten no one, and fear no one, whatever the day brings. Until tomorrow.
